The article places the tree “junto a la entrada al túnel que conduce al ascensor del castillo de Santa Bárbara, en la avenida Juan Bautista Lafora” and says police closed access “desde el Paseíto Ramiro” during the works, i.e. within roughly 100-150m of the already-published ali_011 (the two Paseito de Ramiro figs, register_ids 614/853). No girth, height or exact address given. An Overpass check found two OSM nodes tagged denotation=natural_monument, leaf_cycle=evergreen, leaf_type=broadleaved (ids 10794054257 at 38.3465440,-0.4771636 and 10794054258 at 38.3466555,-0.4770778), roughly 100m east of ali_011's pair and carrying no species or circumference tag and no register_ref, so they are not in data/registers/valencia-arboles-monumentales.json (the register's nearest rows are 614 and 853 themselves, ~95-105m away). Genuinely unresolved whether this news tree IS ali_011 (described loosely, seen from a different vantage point) or a third, separate monumental fig standing nearer the library/tunnel that the Valencia register never captured. Needs: the article's own photo compared against ali_011's crown, or a street-level/satellite look at the tunnel entrance itself, before it can be shipped as anything (confirmation of ali_011, or a new tree with a real pin). Do not re-search this as a news story, the event itself is now fully covered; the open question is purely which trunk it is.

leads.name: Ficus de la Finca La Concepció
leads.reason: CHECKED 2026-08-23: 7.7km from centre, girth 4.8m, height 15.4m, crown 29.5m (Generalitat Valenciana register, category Proteccion Generica). NOT in Alicante municipality: this is the Finca/Casa de la Concepcion in Sant Joan d'Alacant (Carrer Hernan Cortes, 8), a separate town on TRAM line 2, roughly 25 minutes end to end from Luceros plus a walk, so borderline for the day-trip boundary rather than clearly inside it. Turismo Sant Joan's own page (https://turismosantjoan.es/en/la-concepcion-estate/) independently confirms a ficus 'more than 100 years old' on the eastern edge of the property, 'included in the municipal catalog of protected trees', which is a genuine second source for species and a derived age (over a century) alongside the register. That is the good news. Access is the open question: the same page says 'the original perimeter fence has been removed' but 'a recent fence covered with heather surrounds this building', and current ownership plans to convert the historic house into a hostel; a separate search snippet (not independently verified by fetching the page itself) describes the grounds as having 'become a public park'. Those two claims are not flatly contradictory (garden open, building fenced) but this pass could not confirm which side of any fence the ficus stands on, and did not find a source stating opening hours or a free-access line in the terms this project needs for the access field. Hold as a lead: promising (named tree, two sources, real age derivation) but not yet clearable on hard rule 10's access test, and it belongs to a different town's future page as much as to Alicante's, which a later pass should decide with fresh eyes rather than this one guessing under a time box. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-26, no change: fetched a second Turismo Sant Joan page directly ('La Concepcion and Manzaneta Gardens'), which also does not state opening hours, an entry fee or a free-access line, only that 'the gardens have numerous centenary trees that today form part of the most beautiful public park in the municipality' (describing the wider Manzaneta grounds more than confirming which side of a fence this specific ficus sits on). Access still not clearable; do not ship without a source that states hours or an explicit open/closed line for this specific tree's spot.

Register_id 3561 ('Garrofera del Escondite', a named Ceratonia siliqua, height 13.8m, canopy 11.9m) is the one worth flagging specifically: a web search places it in the pedania of Daimes, which belongs to the MUNICIPALITY OF ELCHE, not Alicante, roughly 100 years old per the source, protected under Valencian Law 4/2006 (Prezi deck citing the regional catalogue; not independently fetched/confirmed as a second source this pass). It is a different city's page candidate, not Alicante's, and at 13.35km plus a rural pedania location it would fail this project's day-trip boundary for Alicante regardless. Register_ids 85, 2709 and 2711 (three unnamed Olea europaea, 12.2-12.7km) and 29 ('Palmera imperial', 19.9km) were not individually researched: all sit far past the ~30-minute transit boundary from Alicante centre, none clusters with another candidate or with any published tree, and the pattern set by every other finca-adjacent candidate already checked in this file (private agricultural land, often a ruin) makes a further look low-yield. None of the five is a good next step for Alicante; 3561 may be worth a future Elche pass instead.

CHECKED 2026-08-26: Carrer de l'Esportista Ramon Mendizabal 3, girth 6.2m, height 11m, crown 25m (Proteccion Generica). Cross-checked via OSM (node 13092900356, reg_ref=3099, denotation=natural_monument, protected=yes, figures match the register exactly) which sits inside the bbox of way 153247101, alt_name "Parque del Jardin Botanico" (a public park, San Fernando-Princesa Mercedes neighbourhood). The Spanish Wikipedia article "Parque El Botanico" independently confirms this exact tree (centenarian Ficus macrophylla, city-designated "a monumental tree of local interest") but states plainly: "su tronco se encuentra dentro de una parcela de una urbanizacion privada colindante, aunque la mitad de su copa se extiende hacia el parque" (the TRUNK stands on an adjacent private development parcel, Urbanizacion Gran Ficus, though half the canopy reaches into the public park). Per the hard limit "never deliver a tree ... on private land not genuinely open to visitors; when in doubt, leave it out", this is blocked rather than shipped: the trunk itself is not on public ground, only overhanging canopy is visible from the park side. It may be a legitimate view-only candidate under the wider project's viewing-place doctrine (visible from public park ground, pin marking the viewing spot rather than the trunk), which this verification pass is not positioned to apply; a session with full product context should decide rather than a verify pass guessing. Two sources agree on everything except access: the Valencia register (data/registers/valencia-arboles-monumentales.json, id 3099) and es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parque_El_Botanico.
